_job_encryption: per-job encryption for RESULT bodies (runner/wire/jobcrypto.py). Absent or true: results mirror the arriving job -- encrypted job, encrypted result; with true set explicitly, every result is encrypted. Only literal false encrypts no results. This key governs results only; it never gates acceptance. Acceptance of the HMAC-only (cleartext) job form is off by default: a signed job whose body is not an hp_enc envelope is refused unless the runner was started with --allow-cleartext. That flag is the only switch -- there is deliberately no config key for it.
_mail_tls_required: the draft's Transport Binding requirement (IMAP/SMTP over TLS 1.2+, peer certificate verified) as an option: required by default -- IMAP is implicit TLS with a verifying context, SMTP STARTTLS must verify or the connection fails. Only literal false opens the escape hatch (STARTTLS attempted, certificate unverified, WARN logged); an install with false does not meet the draft's TLS requirement. Confidentiality of the object is the envelope, not this hop. No value enables cleartext mail.
_result_stash: a result is stashed under <base_dir>/outbox/ and the job committed as seen before the first send; a send that fails is retried on later polls, at least result_resend_backoff_sec apart, and given up after result_stash_retention_sec into outbox/failed/ (--inspect outbox lists both); the job is never run twice
_transports: enabled transport extensions (each is a supervised extension program; the core is transport-blind): email (the default, and the test transport), file (a watched folder), nats (core NATS pub/sub), dtls (a DTLS session listener, off unless enabled); see docs/extend/transports.md
_transport_file: file transport folders; empty means <base_dir>/transport-file/inbox and <base_dir>/transport-file/outbox; relative paths resolve against base_dir
_transport_dtls: the DTLS session binding (a binding of protocol version 1): a UDP listener, off unless "dtls" is in transports; the shared secret is the session PSK; ephemeral-only key exchange (forward secrecy enforced)
_dtls_greeting: DTLS greeting disclosure tier: none / family (default) / standard / full; the runner chooses, the client cannot widen it
_pong_platform: the platform card on a ping's result (PROTOCOL.md 3.2): none / family (default: os_family, default_interpreter, protocol_versions) / standard (+ os_release, python_version, runner_version) / full (+ path_tools); the same card and tiers as dtls_greeting; the owner chooses, a job cannot widen it
_transport_nats: core NATS only (no JetStream): job envelopes arrive on the subject; results publish to <result_subject_prefix>.<job_id>. Broker credentials (user/password or token; config keys win over URL userinfo) are this transport's first authorization gate and are REQUIRED unless allow_unauthenticated is true; the HMAC body signature is the second gate
_shared_secret_file: alternative: read the secret from a file instead of inline (mutually exclusive with shared_secret)
_additional_secrets_files: alternative: {"key_id": "/path/to/file"}, mutually exclusive per key with additional_secrets
_extensions_dir: where user extension folders live (docs/extend/extensions.md); empty means <base_dir>/extensions; a relative path resolves against base_dir
_extension_review: the extension review (docs/extend/extensions.md, "The review"): before a sense or transport extension is loaded, its code is read against its manifest -- capabilities declared, entry inside the folder, every .py compiles, no symlinks, no bidi control characters, nothing naming the runner's own state. "enforce" (default) refuses a folder with a high finding like a bad manifest and the agent runs without it; "advisory" loads it and logs the findings; "off" skips the review. Anything else is a config error. Verdicts land in <base_dir>/extension-review.json; --inspect review prints them
_extension_sources: the first time an extension runs, its code and the upstream sources and specs its sources.json declares are fetched in the background for the Oracle (docs/extend/extensions.md, "Sources"): "auto" (default) only when a local model runs the Oracle, so a deterministic box makes no request; true on every box, a Pi Light with no model included; false never. The object form {"fetch", "oracle": "provide"|"withhold", "max_mb" (default 512), "unpinned" (default false: an entry no lock pins waits until the owner allows trust on first use), "extensions": {name: {"fetch", "oracle", "unpinned"}}} sets the disclosure rule, the disk budget, the unpinned rule, and per-extension overrides. Read live.
_local_signals: local delivery for senses on this machine (docs/extend/extensions.md): producers drop signed envelopes into <base_dir>/local-inbox or push them to a loopback listener; same signature checks as the mail path, no mailbox involved; false turns both front-ends off; read at startup
_local_signal_port: loopback TCP port for direct-push local signals; 0 or false turns the listener off (the inbox still works); read at startup
_local_wake_cooldown_sec: minimum seconds between Oracle wake briefings for the same sensor+signal; a high or critical locally filed alert wakes the Oracle, which writes its assessment to oracle-briefs.jsonl in the base dir
_oracle_mode: llm (the default) lets the Oracle use the local model in the inference block below. deterministic is the Pi Light mode: no model is installed or ever called, and the Oracle's duties still run -- wake briefs, the watch, answers -- with briefs and answers assembled from the box's own records (the job index, retained jobs, notable lines, the log tail) instead of a model's narration. The pi-light install profile sets this. Flip it back to llm and set up inference to give the same install a model later; nothing else changes.
_oracle_opinion_mode: the Oracle's opinion on each result (PROTOCOL 3.2): off | diagnose | advise | repair (default). This key is both the default latitude for jobs that grant none and the owner's ceiling; a job may request a latitude with its own oracle_opinion member, never above this. diagnose speaks only after a failure, with the obvious cause; advise adds a tier-1 prediction before the run; repair may also replace an absent interpreter with the platform default (never silent: the result says what changed and carries the received job's digest). Repair-by-default covers only the deterministic tier's one mechanical fix -- an absent interpreter swapped for the platform default when the script's shape fits that default -- and the repaired job is always re-judged and re-checked against the key policy before it runs. The model tier is separate: it stays gated by oracle_opinion_model (default false, below), and this default does not enable it. The runner flag --oracle-opinion overrides it for one process.
_oracle_opinion_predict: when tier-1 predictions are computed: requested (default; only when the job requests advise or repair within the ceiling) | always (every job gets a prediction under advise semantics) | never. Diagnose needs no prediction and runs on any failure at diagnose latitude or higher, whatever this says.
_oracle_opinion_model: tier-2 opinion: when true and inference is configured, the local model may add a labeled note ('Model-formed note:') to an opinion tier 1 had nothing to say about. Default false. In deterministic oracle_mode no model is ever called, so tier-1 opinions still file on a Pi Light box and tier 2 stays dark.
_oracle_opinion_repair: how a repair is authorized: rejudge (default; the repaired job goes back through the judge and the key policy exactly as a received job would, and if it is refused the original job's failure result is returned with the opinion explaining) | refuse (repairs are never executed; the opinion degrades to advise and describes the proposed fix).
_oracle_learning: the Oracle's self-learning loop (docs/design/oracle-opinion-design.md): every opinion call is frozen before the job runs, scored against the verified outcome the moment the job finishes, and written to oracle-learning.jsonl in the base dir; the next job's opinion evaluation reads the ledger fresh, so lessons are in view with no restart. Lessons come in two kinds: verified facts derived by code from execution records (trusted, keyed to this host), and -- only with oracle_learning_model below -- model-distilled candidates, labeled uncorroborated until later verified outcomes promote them. A lesson never authorizes anything by itself: repairs still require the repair latitude, a precondition re-verified on the current job, and re-judgment. Default true; false turns the loop off entirely (nothing recorded, nothing used). At oracle_opinion_mode off, nothing is recorded or used either.
_oracle_learning_model: the model channel of the learning loop: when true AND oracle_opinion_model is true AND inference is configured, the local model may distill one schema-validated candidate lesson from a failed or mispredicted job's outcome and output. Candidates are hypotheses -- labeled uncorroborated wherever they surface -- until verified outcomes corroborate them (oracle_learning_promote_after). Default false. In deterministic oracle_mode no model is ever called, so a Pi Light box learns verified facts only.
_oracle_learning_promote_after: how many verified corroborating outcomes a model candidate needs before it is treated as corroborated and may select among the existing mechanical repairs (it still never drives one alone: the repair's preconditions are re-verified on the current job and the repaired job is re-judged). A single verified contradiction retires a candidate as negative evidence. Default 2.
_remediation_mode: remediation (docs/design/remediation-design.md): what the runner does when a running job diverges from the intent envelope its opinion recorded. off | deterministic (default) | oracle. off watches, records, and pages only -- the human decides. deterministic arms the closed tripwire list (confinement escape, process storm past the ceiling, an undeclared credential-store reference in a produced artifact): those kill the job's tree on sight, quarantine its outputs, refer suspect files to the box's antivirus, and page the owner. oracle additionally lets the local model order a kill for a lesser divergence; anything short of an affirmative order is an abstention and never kills. A job cannot request, widen, or narrow remediation; it is owner configuration only. The runner flag --remediation-mode overrides it for one process.
_remediation_storm_ceiling: the process-storm tripwire: a job whose process tree grows past this many processes is killed on sight. A named constant with a config knob, not a heuristic.
_remediation_sample_sec: how often the per-job remediation monitor samples the running job's process tree and workdir, in seconds. Deliberately independent of the mailbox poll cadence: most jobs are shorter than one poll cycle.
_remediation_oracle_timeout_sec: the bound on the Oracle's remediation judgment call in oracle mode. A timeout is an abstention: the job keeps running, and the abstention is recorded.
_remediation_quarantine_max_jobs: quarantine bounds: at most this many seized jobs are held in <base_dir>/quarantine; older seizures are archived (moved, never deleted) to quarantine-archive/.
_remediation_quarantine_max_bytes: quarantine bounds: at most this many bytes of seized outputs are held before the oldest are archived (moved, never deleted).
_dag_mode: off (the default) lists a task's dependencies in its description and trusts the worker. advisory hands a task out even when its requires are incomplete, with a dag_warning naming them on the offer and in the log. enforce withholds the task until every requirement is done. Any other value behaves as off.
_verbose: "verbose": true turns on the decision lines in runner.log -- poll cycles, ingest accepts and rejects with reasons, wake-gate scores against the threshold, judge verdicts, board offers -- the same lines -v adds for one process. "verbose": false quiets the log like --quiet. The command line (-v / --quiet) wins either way, and editing the key live takes effect on the next poll cycle. Absent (as here) is the base level: the log the runner has always printed.

_comments.detection: Optional low-overhead detection (runner/oracle/detection.py) runs after job completion when the module is importable. It records detection_hits (Sigma/YARA-style rules + ATT&CK tags), detection_anomaly (tiny baseline), and plan_budget_ok when a job carries a plan list. Canary tripwires are separate (_canary_watch). All advisory; never raises.
